claim_text: Stack Overflow 2026: 48.0% selected trust when output is easily verified (n=14304); 76.5% selected running output locally before use (n=13162).
notes: Different questions and bases; validation is multi-select; not an estimate of all coding-agent users.

claim_text: The Stack Overflow 2026 methodology reports 30903 valid responses across 169 countries, recruited through community sites, blog and email.
unit: valid survey responses and countries represented
notes: Non-probability recruitment; no global population weights established.

claim_text: GitLab/Harris release: 85% agreed the bottleneck shifted to review/validation; 80% said adoption outran policy; 98% allocated or expected governance budget; sample 1528 in six countries.
unit: percent of respondents as summarized by sponsor
notes: Self-reported attitudes and intentions; not purchases, demand for sandbox software or market penetration.

claim_text: Sonar reports 59% rated review/correction effort moderate or substantial and 38% found AI code harder to review than human code; online sample n=1149, fielded October 2025.
unit: percent of eligible surveyed AI-using technology workers
notes: Report year 2026 is not field year; self-reported effort, not measured time.

claim_text: METR cautions that its 2026 productivity follow-up is unreliable for current effects because of participant/task selection and parallel-agent time measurement.
notes: Do not reuse early-2025 slowdown as a universal current estimate.

claim_text: Stripe describes standardized isolated devboxes and deterministic lint/test workflow stages for its internal coding agents.
notes: First-party implementation account; dollar spend and willingness to buy INVARIANT unknown.

claim_text: Ramp describes agent sessions with development services, integrations and output verification; it built an internal background agent.
notes: Full account available in search-index rendering; direct page rendered only tagline. No numerical adoption claim used.

claim_text: E2B reports Lark selected its execution infrastructure for isolated application tests and Docker support, reducing the need to build infrastructure internally.
notes: Vendor-selected account; contract amount and independently verified savings unavailable.

claim_text: Stack Overflow 2026: better output quality was the primary switching reason for 25.1%, compared with security/privacy/compliance for 2.2%; n=13144 includes nonswitchers.
unit: percent of all respondents to switching question, not switchers only
notes: Broad AI products, not just agents; not willingness to pay or prevalence of security concerns.

claim_text: Docker describes persistent local microVM agent environments, protected host access, domain policy, credential injection, and a private-clone workspace option.
notes: Documented features; no independent efficacy benchmark. Contradictory skills-default wording excluded.

claim_text: Docker states local sbx CLI/compute is free including commercial use; cloud/model costs are separate; AI Governance is separately sold per license through sales.
notes: AI Governance numeric list price not published in reviewed plan page; not assumed zero.

claim_text: E2B documents microVM execution and pause/snapshot/fork lifecycle; pricing lists Hobby free plus usage and Pro USD150/month plus usage.
unit: USD per billing unit and term stated in claim; accompanying features are documentary claims
notes: Different product/edition and billing basis from local CLI; storage/limits not normalized.

claim_text: Daytona documents lifecycle operations and reusable sandbox infrastructure; pricing lists CPU USD0.0504/vCPU-hour and RAM USD0.0162/GiB-hour, plus storage.
unit: USD per billing unit and term stated in claim; accompanying features are documentary claims
notes: Per-second billing; backend/default edition descriptions conflict across indexed versions; no security equivalence asserted.

claim_text: Sprites describes persistent whole-filesystem checkpoints and credential connectors; lists USD0.0385/CPU-hour and USD0.021875/memory-GB-hour plus storage.
unit: USD per billing unit and term stated in claim; accompanying features are documentary claims
notes: Usage metering differs from allocated cloud resources; current list price is not a workload cost benchmark.

claim_text: Claude documents native shell sandbox controls and managed settings; checkpoint rewind excludes Bash-created changes.
notes: Sandbox coverage varies by tool/platform/settings; do not generalize shell isolation to MCP and file tools.

claim_text: Claude pricing lists Pro USD20 monthly or USD200 annually and includes Claude Code, subject to usage limits.
unit: USD per billing unit and term stated in claim; accompanying features are documentary claims
notes: Advertised rounded monthly equivalent differs slightly from 200/12; annual total preserved; tax/usage excluded.

claim_text: OpenAI describes Codex approvals, managed requirements, network policies and OpenTelemetry event export; help page says Codex is included across ChatGPT plans with varying limits.
notes: Vendor internal deployment account and current entitlements; not a guarantee every installation matches that deployment.

claim_text: Gemini documents sandbox providers and permission expansion; pricing documents eligible free tiers and separate paid subscription/usage options.
notes: Account/service eligibility and current quotas apply; not unlimited free inference.

claim_text: Development Containers defines development environment configuration; Microsoft allows personal and corporate use of Remote Development extensions on owned machines or containers.
notes: Runtime/hosting may cost money; this is not proof every devcontainer is an agent security boundary.

claim_text: NVIDIA OpenShell v0.1.4 documents declarative sandbox policy, runtime network changes and credential controls; its runtime is available as open source.
notes: Commercial support price unknown in reviewed pages; no independent security certification implied.

claim_text: CodeRabbit displayed annual-billing view lists Essentials USD24, Team USD48 and Advanced USD72 per user/month, with review capabilities and usage restrictions.
unit: USD per billing unit and term stated in claim; accompanying features are documentary claims
notes: Other products, monthly-billing prices and consumption costs separate; feature efficacy not independently measured.

claim_text: Git worktrees provide separate working trees; git restore restores selected version-controlled paths rather than an installed Linux environment.
notes: Not a sandbox or complete backup; does not undo external service effects.

claim_text: Current INVARIANT documents a persistent Linux/Codex environment with protected inspection; the saved real-project report records 11 passed migration/resume/guardrail checks.
unit: passed checks in one saved verification report
notes: Saved evidence inspected, not rerun in this research. One tested environment, not general production assurance.

claim_text: INVARIANT architecture documents direct project mounting, none/internet networking, separate project/checkpoint data, and absent disk quotas/export/garbage collection.
notes: Read-only local assessment; broad internet access is not package-only access; persist does not mean joint rollback.

claim_text: The invoice broker contract limits target operations and excludes real enterprise credentials and production multi-tenant security from that profile.
notes: A mock adapter is not an enterprise API authorization product.

claim_text: Current alternatives already document isolation, persistence, network controls and several recovery mechanisms, so a new implementation alone is not evidence of differentiation.
notes: Analyst synthesis; not a claim that all products are feature-equivalent.

claim_text: The clearest broad problem in reviewed evidence is verification/review of AI output; control is important but a separately purchased INVARIANT product is unvalidated.
notes: Problem evidence stronger than product demand; sponsor selection and self-report limit generalization.

claim_text: Conditionally prioritize small-team reproducible verification and handoff; rank controlled team execution second and standalone personal recovery environments third.
notes: Ranking is judgment about entry feasibility, not measured market size, prevalence or sales probability.

claim_text: Test engineering leads at teams of 10-50 developers using at least two coding-agent products as an initial customer hypothesis.
notes: Target size and multi-agent requirement chosen for recruitment; not an observed optimal segment.

claim_text: Test USD200 per team/month for up to ten active users, with compute and model charges excluded, only after observing workflow value.
notes: Experimental offer, not validated willingness to pay or competitor-normalized market price.

claim_text: Proceed only through the stated interview, comparative pilot, safety and paid-renewal gates; otherwise stop or revise the target.
notes: Predeclared decision rules are management choices, not empirical findings.

claim_text: Research used the market-research-reports skill; the verified attribution is Kassis, Agarwal, He, Patel and Brueckner (2026), Scientific Agent Skills, arXiv:2609.00065, current v2.
notes: Methodology attribution only; excluded from market evidence.
